input.question: why haven't we evolved stronger teeth?
input.ground_truth: If our teeth were not good enough to hang in while we bred and raised our young until they were self-sufficient, we would have developed better teeth. Evolutionary adaptations don't happen because it helps us survive. It happens because it helps us live long enough to reproduce and take care of our offspring until *our offspring* can survive. tl;dr: your teeth last until your DNA is done with you.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why haven't we evolved stronger teeth?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your teeth are like the tools you use to eat your favorite snacks. Our bodies have changed over a long, long time because of what we eat and how we live.

Long ago, people ate really tough food, like roots and leaves. So, their teeth got stronger because they had to chew hard things all the time. But now, we eat softer food, like bananas, bread, and pasta. We also have things like forks and spoons to help us eat.

Because we don’t need super strong teeth anymore (thanks to our tools and soft food), our bodies didn’t need to make them even stronger. So, our teeth stayed just strong enough to help us eat the food we have now. That’s why we haven’t evolved even stronger teeth!
